item.title: REF 0.26.0
item.description:
• The notes now say only what's true of your files: fixes for the quieter, louder and true-peak notes, the clip count, reference sets and the 10-octave layout.
  • A message line under the songs says what went wrong, in plain words, even with nothing loaded. Nothing fails silently any more.
  • A file REF can't read says why, and you can click it to pick another.
  • Dropping two files on Your mix uses the first and leaves your reference alone. Taking out an unsaved set has an Undo.
  • "Follow plug-in" keeps your mix until the plug-in's first print arrives.
  • Drop a song anywhere on the empty window to start.
  • Units everywhere: tile differences, charts and song numbers say LU, dB or pts, and against a set they say "the set".
  • On the Tone tab, "over" and "under" mean the distance outside the set's range.
  • Help › Keyboard Shortcuts lists every key. The Playback menu names them too.
  • One name for a saved set, in every menu and message.
  • Settings: True peak, Clipped samples and Streaming service moved to Notes; Restore Defaults asks first; Look has a Larger text size.
  • Bigger reference slot cells, with a mark on a slot whose file failed.
  • VoiceOver reads buttons, notes, slots and meters by name.
  • Linear-phase Match EQ now plays narrow low bands as drawn (it runs about 0.7 s late; minimum phase, the default, has no delay).
  • Band names show the compared range (sub from 30 Hz), mono files say they're measured as dual mono, and "Thinnest at" no longer points at breakdowns.
  • A silent file, or one with a silent channel, gets one clear note.
